articles.title: 121st Field Hospital Revives Korean War-Era Rail Evacuation With a Commercial Railcar

articles.title: TACOM welcomes newest Hall of Fame inductees
articles.summary: Smiles, hugs and happy tears filled the Detroit Arsenal as five people who spent decades shaping the U.S. Army Tank-automotive and Armaments Command took a permanent place in its history. Agnes E. Holley-Smith, David W. Horton, Michele M. Moore, James “Patton” Tidwell and David L. Van Agtmael were inducted Oct. 28 into the TACOM Hall of Fame.

articles.title: Mobile Army Surgical Hospitals: A history of saving lives on the battlefield
articles.summary: During World War II, the U.S. Army opened its first Mobile Army Surgical Hospitals, changing the way the wounded were treated in battle for several decades — saving lives and increasing warfighter readiness. Combining mobility, surgery, and post-op care, MASH units were known as the front-line surgical hospitals of the future.

Beard, Jr., 23, who was captured and died as a prisoner of war during World War II, will be interred Nov. 11 at Holston View Cemetery in Weber City, near his hometown of Fort Blackmore, Virginia. Services and interment are being coordinated by Fischer Funeral Services 276-594-1874.
